name: Opensteer

modes.label: Browser / computer runtime (per hour)
modes.note: Published 'browser runtime $0.20/hr' and 'computer runtime $0.20/hr' (opensteer.com/pricing, 2026-09-28). Machine size (vCPU/RAM), billing granularity and concurrency are not published. Platform credits ($5/$50/$200 per month) cover 'browsers and computers'; model credits are separate and not counted.

plans.name: Developer
plans.note: Free. $5/mo platform credits (browsers and computers, = 25 runtime-hours at $0.20/h); '$5 model credits to start' (one-off) not counted as compute. Limited to 3 agents; core models at capped effort; BYO Claude/ChatGPT subscription.

plans.name: Starter
plans.note: $50/mo platform credits; $25/mo model credits not counted.

plans.name: Business
plans.note: $200/mo platform credits; $100/mo model credits not counted.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom onboarding and environment setup, SLAs and dedicated support, spend controls and observability. Price not published.

features.ip_note: Local Chrome/Edge or Opensteer Cloud browsers; proxy/egress IP type not documented.

caveats: Priced as $0.20 per browser- or computer-runtime hour with no published machine size; the workload vCPU/RAM is not guaranteed. Platform credits offset runtime; model credits do not.

Browser and computer runtime each $0.20/h. Model and platform credits are distinct; $5/$25/$100 model credits must not offset compute. BYO Claude/ChatGPT subscription agent claim does not establish free underlying 4/8 VM.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.

fleet.notes: Pricing counts agent identities and separates model/platform credits. Unlimited agents on paid plans is not documented unlimited browser/computer capacity; numeric active-machine quotas and increase process not found.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

image_oci.quote: Use Opensteer Cloud when an agent should live 24/7 on a managed server with hosted workspaces, schedules, browser profiles, security controls, and team access.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Opensteer Cloud provisions fixed agent workspaces (browser/computer runtime), not custom-image machine hosting.

nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — the runtime is a browser/computer-use agent workspace, not a general VM/emulation platform.

desktop.note: A distinct billed 'computer runtime' alongside 'browser runtime' implies a full desktop/computer environment beyond the browser; not further documented (no VNC/RDP details published).

computer_use.note: Billed 'computer runtime' distinct from 'browser runtime' implies a computer-use (screenshot/click) capability; the Python helpers already expose click_at_xy/type_text/screenshots for the browser, and 'computer runtime' extends this beyond the browser.

captcha_solving.quote: Specialized AI agents that do real work. They browse the web, use your tools, and run on schedules, in the cloud or on your machine.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no CAPTCHA-solving service is documented.

ssh.quote: opensteer-run is the local agent's remote toolbelt for commands and file operations; it does not use SSH, Daytona IDs, or a local workspace mirror.
ssh.note: Access to the hosted workspace is explicitly via opensteer-run (exec/read/write/patch), not SSH.

persistent_disk.quote:
opensteer-cloud profiles create "LinkedIn"
opensteer-cloud profiles sync LinkedIn --browser chrome --domain linkedin.com
persistent_disk.note: Hosted agent workspaces persist browser profiles and 24/7 state across sessions per the open-source page ('live 24/7 on a managed server with hosted workspaces ... browser profiles').

agent_harnesses.quote: Templates are starter harnesses we built for common agent patterns. Copy one, fill in the setup, and customize the skills and scripts for your workflow.

harness_api.quote:
opensteer-cloud attach <agent>
opensteer-run exec "pytest"
opensteer-run read skills/SKILL.md
opensteer-run write actions/job.py < /tmp/job.py
harness_api.note: The cloud CLI drives a coding harness (attach a local coding agent like Codex/Claude Code, run/read/write/patch files) inside the hosted workspace.

own_agent_api.quote:
opensteer-cloud agent create "linkedin sales"
opensteer-cloud agent list
own_agent_api.note: First-party API/CLI to create and manage Opensteer's own hosted browser/computer-use agents.

lang_python.quote: Opensteer helps AI agents control browsers and use local code as tools. It gives agents a small Python command surface for local Chrome or Edge, Opensteer Cloud browsers, and project-specific automation.

gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — pricing lists only browser/computer runtime and managed-model usage, no GPU machines.

windows.quote: There is no desktop build for this platform in the current release.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — that line refers to the local desktop client, not a Windows cloud machine; no Windows machine offering is documented for Opensteer Cloud.

macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — hosted runtimes are Linux-based browser/computer agent workspaces; no macOS cloud machine is documented.

byoc.quote: Enterprise — Custom onboarding and environment setup · SLAs and dedicated support · Spend controls and observability
byoc.note: Even Enterprise is described as custom onboarding/support, not deployment into the customer's own cloud account; not offered as documented.

docker_inside.quote: Opensteer helps AI agents control browsers and use local code as tools. It gives agents a small Python command surface for local Chrome or Edge, Opensteer Cloud browsers, and project-specific automation.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Opensteer is a CDP browser-control + Python tool-calling runtime, not a general container/Docker host.

fork.quote: List and select browsers without creating a new one: opensteer -c "print(list_browsers())"
fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — the unit of work is named browser sessions/profiles, not clonable machines; no fork/clone concept documented.

fork_running.quote: mode='reuse' is the safe default. mode='new' intentionally creates another logical session.
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no machine-cloning concept exists to fork while running.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: mode='reuse' is the safe default. mode='new' intentionally creates another logical session.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no clone/fork capability of any kind is documented.

volume_attach.quote: Use Opensteer Cloud when an agent should live 24/7 on a managed server with hosted workspaces, schedules, browser profiles, security controls, and team access.
volume_attach.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no attachable block/persistent-volume feature is documented; state is workspace/browser-profile data.

volume_shared.quote: Use Opensteer Cloud when an agent should live 24/7 on a managed server with hosted workspaces, schedules, browser profiles, security controls, and team access.
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no multi-machine shared-volume concept is documented.

live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no CPU/RAM sizing is exposed to customers at all (billed as flat per-runtime-hour), so there is nothing to live-resize.

mcp_server.quote: Browser / Opensteer Cloud -> CDP websocket -> Opensteer daemon -> opensteer -c
mcp_server.note: not offered: control surface is a Python CLI/daemon over CDP with an HTTP/API key model; no MCP server is mentioned on opensteer.com or in the GitHub org.

lang_node.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — the SDK/CLI (`opensteer.helpers`, `uv tool install opensteer`) is Python-only; no Node.js runtime or SDK is documented.

public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — the runtimes are accessed via CDP/API for agent browser and computer control, not as general machines exposing a public IPv4 for hosted apps.

inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no feature for exposing HTTPS URLs to ports on the runtime is documented; access is via the Opensteer CLI/daemon and cloud API.

ingress_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — there is no inbound-port hosting feature to apply ingress rules to.

guest_firewall.quote: Opensteer is an open-source runtime for local AI agents. It gives Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and other coding agents browser control plus a simple way to call code from the current project.
guest_firewall.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no root/guest-OS access to the cloud runtime is documented (it is a browser/code-tool automation surface, not a general VM), so no basis to derive guest firewall access.

arm64.note: not offered: machine architecture is fully abstracted away (flat per-runtime-hour pricing with no vCPU/RAM/arch selection); no ARM64 option is exposed to customers.

anti_bot.quote: Opensteer is an open-source runtime for local AI agents. It gives Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and other coding agents browser control plus a simple way to call code from the current project.
anti_bot.note: not offered: no stealth/anti-fingerprinting or bot-detection-evasion feature is documented anywhere in the product's docs, README, or pricing page.

snapshot.quote: Use Opensteer Cloud when an agent should live 24/7 on a managed server with hosted workspaces, schedules, browser profiles, security controls, and team access.
snapshot.note: Persistence is described via always-on hosted workspaces and synced browser profiles, not VM/disk/memory snapshot or checkpoint APIs; no snapshot feature is documented.

snapshot_auto.quote: Use Opensteer Cloud when an agent should live 24/7 on a managed server with hosted workspaces, schedules, browser profiles, security controls, and team access.
snapshot_auto.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — workspaces are always-on hosted servers, not stop/start machines with automatic state save/restore.

snapshot_on_demand.quote:
opensteer-cloud agent create "linkedin sales"
opensteer-cloud agent list
snapshot_on_demand.note: not offered: the cloud CLI exposes agent/profile creation and file-level exec/read/write/patch, no snapshot/checkpoint command is documented.

pause_resume.quote: Use Opensteer Cloud when an agent should live 24/7 on a managed server with hosted workspaces, schedules, browser profiles, security controls, and team access.
pause_resume.note: not offered: hosted agent workspaces are described as running 24/7; no pause/resume (billing-paused) machine state is documented.

wake_on_request.quote: Use Opensteer Cloud when an agent should live 24/7 on a managed server with hosted workspaces, schedules, browser profiles, security controls, and team access.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: workspaces are positioned as always-on ('live 24/7'), not sleeping machines that wake on an incoming request.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Use Opensteer Cloud when an agent should live 24/7 on a managed server with hosted workspaces, schedules, browser profiles, security controls, and team access.
auto_stop_idle.note: not offered: the product markets 24/7 always-on hosted workspaces rather than idle-triggered stop/sleep; no auto-stop-on-idle behavior is documented.

secret_proxy.quote: OPENSTEER_BROWSER_ID plus OPENSTEER_API_KEY lets the daemon stop a cloud browser on shutdown.
secret_proxy.note: Authentication to Opensteer's own API is via an env-var API key; no first-party proxy that injects third-party HTTP API credentials into the sandbox is documented.

max_session_h.quote: Use Opensteer Cloud when an agent should live 24/7 on a managed server with hosted workspaces, schedules, browser profiles, security controls, and team access.
max_session_h.note: Hosted agent workspaces are marketed as running 24/7 with no published maximum session length; billed per runtime-hour with no time cap documented.

usage_api.quote: browser runtime $0.20/hr, computer runtime $0.20/hr. Platform credits offset runtime; no per-sandbox usage reporting API documented.
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: no; Opensteer's pricing and CLI docs describe flat per-runtime-hour billing and agent/profile management, but do not document a programmatic usage API (REST, SDK, or CLI) to query billable usage per sandbox, per tag, or per project. The opensteer-cloud CLI controls agent lifecycle and file operations, not usage reporting.
